name: involve.me
tagline: Build an interactive quiz or calculator and capture its results

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: 2 live funnels; 50 submissions/month or 500 visits/month; 30-day data retention; 1 user; 100MB storage; 2MB maximum file; 1 website; 0 AI credits
tiers.notes: At the cap, funnels lock until the next calendar month.

tiers.name: Start
tiers.limits: 3 live funnels, 1 user, 50 AI credits/month, 500MB storage, 20MB maximum file, 1 payment platform and 1 website

tiers.name: Grow
tiers.limits: 5 live funnels, 2 users, 100 AI credits/month, 1GB storage, 50MB maximum file, 1 custom domain, 2 payment platforms and 1 website

tiers.name: Scale
tiers.limits: 25 live funnels, 5 users, 300 AI credits/month, 5GB storage, 200MB maximum file, 3 custom domains, 10 payment platforms and 3 websites

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Custom funnels, traffic, submissions, users, retention, storage, domains, payment platforms and websites
tiers.notes: Annual contracts only; published as starting from $499/month.

pricing.freeTierCaps: 2 live funnels; 50 submissions/month or 500 visits/month; 30-day retention; 1 user; 100MB storage; 2MB maximum file; 1 website; 0 AI credits
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual prepaid (up to 40% off); Enterprise is annual-contract only; 14-day premium trial requires a card and auto-converts unless canceled
pricing.hiddenCosts: Extra seats cost $10/user/month on Grow and Scale, and extra custom domains cost $10/month. EU VAT is extra. Paid-plan submission caps are not disclosed on the current public pricing page.

verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For involve.me, build an interactive quiz or calculator and capture its results. The hard boundary is templates, conditional content, calculations, lead integrations, and analytics, plus integrations, deliverability, and workflow depth.
coreLoopDIY: Build a public interactive quiz, calculator, or form, validate submissions, notify the owner, and provide a private response table with CSV export.
requirements: Resend API key or SMTP credentials
whatYouLose: templates, conditional content, calculations, lead integrations, and analytics
ongoingBurden: spam control, email delivery, storage, exports, accessibility, conditional logic, and integrations
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for involve.me because a basic form is trivial; people pay when the form feeds a dependable business workflow and never loses a response. The recurring cost buys spam control, email delivery, storage, exports, accessibility, conditional logic, and integrations, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Formbricks
priorArt.desc: Active open-source survey and experience-management platform.

alternatives.name: Forminator
alternatives.desc: Forms, polls, quizzes, calculations, and payments, free as long as you already live inside WordPress

facts.install: Install and activate the Forminator plugin from WordPress Admin
facts.dataFormat: Forms and submissions are stored in the site's WordPress database; uploaded files are stored in WordPress uploads, and submissions can be exported as CSV.
facts.gapVsPaid: Forminator covers forms, polls, quizzes, calculations, and payments, but WordPress is mandatory and its outcome-funnel analytics and presentation are weaker than involve.me's.
facts.setupBlocker: It only runs inside an existing WordPress site, so hosting, WordPress maintenance and mail delivery must already be solved.

alternatives.name: Typebot
alternatives.desc: Conversational forms with serious branching; free to self-host, fair-source, and not a weekend Docker toy

facts.install: Hosted signup, or Docker Compose/manual deployment of builder and viewer
facts.engines: Connects to OpenAI, Anthropic, Mistral, ElevenLabs and Dify through built-in integration blocks; API credentials are supplied by the user
facts.dataFormat: Hosted bots and results live in Typebot Cloud; self-hosted data lives in PostgreSQL and uploaded files in S3-compatible object storage.
facts.gapVsPaid: Typebot has serious branching, variables, and integrations, but its conversational interface is less purpose-built for polished quiz outcomes, calculator result pages, and marketing reports.
facts.setupBlocker: Self-hosting requires PostgreSQL, S3-compatible storage, two web apps, DNS/TLS and mail/auth configuration; the licence is Fair Source rather than OSI open source.

alternatives.name: Tally
alternatives.desc: A very generous free form builder; branding and custom domains are the tax

facts.engines: Tally AI is available, but its underlying model provider is not publicly documented
facts.dataFormat: Forms and responses live in Tally's EU-hosted cloud; responses can be downloaded as CSV or synchronized to Google Sheets or Notion.
facts.gapVsPaid: Tally handles quizzes, logic, and calculations cleanly, but result segmentation, funnel analytics, custom domains, and branding control are much lighter or paid compared with involve.me.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Starter plan and a single-owner form service DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for involve.me in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, SQLite, Drizzle ORM, and Resend; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: build a public interactive quiz, calculator, or form, validate submissions, notify the owner, and provide a private response table with CSV export.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Create a form builder with short text, long text, email, number, select, radio, checkbox, and file fields.
Publish each form at a stable slug with server-side validation and accessible labels.
Add honeypot, rate limiting, submission-size limits, and a clear privacy notice.
Store responses in SQLite and provide search, filters, detail view, and CSV export.
Send an owner notification without placing submitted values in logs.
Support a thank-you screen and one simple conditional branch.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out payment collection.
Deliberately leave out hundreds of third-party integrations.
Deliberately leave out multi-brand enterprise workspaces and compliance attestations.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
